title: Rare Knowledge Mining Methodological Framework (RKMMF) for developing rare-disease clinical training
description: The RKMMF is a phased methodological framework the article uses to structure development of clinical evaluator training in rare disease care. It proceeds through a preliminary needs assessment — described as "an essential step prior to implementing RKMMF-informed workshops" — followed by knowledge mining with expert content leads, group sharing with medical experts to validate findings, external validation via pre-workshop surveys adapted from the Kirkpatrick model, and knowledge translation with post-workshop evaluation. The article demonstrates it as "a scalable approach for capacity-building in rare disease care".
requirements: A needs assessment must be conducted prior to implementing RKMMF-informed workshops to align the intervention with the target audience's real-world challenges
constraints: Demonstrated in the Canadian SMA clinical context with PTs, OTs and nurses; the article notes some insights were directly related to Canada
target_learners: clinical evaluators: physiotherapists, occupational therapists, and neuromuscular nurses
target_learning_goals: selecting, administering and interpreting clinical outcome assessments in spinal muscular atrophy
examples: Two bilingual SMA COA workshops were developed and delivered using the framework's phases, with 79 participants and pre/post survey evaluation
